findings.title: A swallowed read error is reported as a doctype failure (exit 1), not exit 2
findings.description: `validateFile` calls `parseFrontmatter(file)` at line 95 and never checks `frontmatter.found`. That parser has a blanket catch that converts *any* read failure into `{ found: false, data: {} }` (`packages/core/src/introspection/parsers/frontmatterParser.ts:63-64`). So if a file disappears, changes permissions, or errors on read after `preflight` (`:72-86`) succeeded, the early return at `:96-98` emits `{ pass: false, missing: [], reason: 'doctype' }` instead of an error. The CLI then prints `FAIL <file>` plus the frontmatter message and exits 1 — exactly the "partial results alongside an error" and wrong-exit-code case the file header (`:1-8`) and slice 214's success criteria say must be exit 2 with empty stdout. The `readFile` catch at `:102-105` cannot help: it is unreachable on this path. The same file is also read twice (`:95`, `:102`), which widens that race; a legitimate no-frontmatter document also returns `found: false`, so checking `found` alone cannot separate it from an I/O failure. Read the file once with explicit error handling and parse frontmatter from that text, then add a fault-injection regression test for a read failure after preflight (the existing `sliceDesignFiles.test.ts` only covers failures caught by preflight).

findings.title: `--json` error mode is derived from raw argv, so the command's `-j` alias emits plain-text errors
findings.description: `withJsonOption` (`packages/cli/src/options.ts`) registers `-j, --json`, but `handleError` at `:104` decides its output format from a module-level flag (`packages/cli/src/utils/errors.ts:32-38,47`) that is set only by `packages/cli/src/index.ts:178` via `process.argv.includes('--json')`. `cf validate design -j missing.md` therefore produces JSON results on stdout for successful runs but a human `Error: ...` line on stderr for exit-2 failures, contradicting the structured-error contract in `docs/AGENT-INTEGRATION.md:16` that makes this command a machine gate. `CF_JSON=1` hides the problem, which is why it only shows up for flag-driven use. There are now two sources of truth for "is this a JSON invocation" (parsed `opts.json` vs. global argv sniffing); derive the error mode from the parsed option (or detect `-j` as well) so the alias behaves identically.

findings.title: The machine-readable failure path is never asserted by the new command tests
findings.description: The `run()` helper (`:127-131`) registers `registerValidateCommand` on a bare `Command` and never imports `packages/cli/src/index.ts`, so `setJsonMode()` is never called and `handleError` always takes its plain-text branch in this suite. The six `--json` exit-2 cases (`:205-211`) assert only `cf exited 2`, empty stdout and empty `console.log`; no test asserts that stderr carries `{ "error": true, ... }`, and the one error-message assertion (`:216-222`) runs without `--json`. Consequently neither the documented JSON error payload nor the post-preflight I/O failure mode from the first finding has any regression coverage, even though `--json` is the primary agent/CI interface for this command. Add a case that enables JSON error mode (as the real entrypoint does) and pins the stderr payload for `--json` and `-j` failures, plus a case that fails a read after preflight.

structured_findings.summary: A swallowed read error is reported as a doctype failure (exit 1), not exit 2
`--json` error mode is derived from raw argv, so the command's `-j` alias emits plain-text errors
The machine-readable failure path is never asserted by the new command tests
